messages:
kyle: quick check — rolling out feature_x. If org-level flag is OFF and project 'payments' sets feature_x to ON for a 10% canary, but a specific route /v2/checkout has an explicit OFF, which wins? don't want to accidentally turn it back on for checkout.
anita: short answer: the most-specific explicit setting wins. scope order is model/route > project > org. so a route-level OFF will block /v2/checkout even if project-level canary would include the user.
samir: nuance: canary audiences and percentage rollouts are evaluated when a scope provides them, but they don't override an explicit boolean at a more-specific scope. if route has no config, project canary may enable you; if route says OFF explicitly, that stops it.
kyle: ok — so explicit null/undefined at route -> fallthrough to project; explicit false at route -> deny. good to know.
taylor: another edge: project has 10% rollout, route has an audience rule (e.g., teammates) that includes you. do they combine or is one authoritative?
anita: we treat audiences/rollouts as evaluable conditions at their scope. algorithmically: check scopes from most-specific to least; if you hit an explicit boolean, return it. if you hit a rollout/audience, evaluate and return result. otherwise fallthrough. so if route has an audience that returns true, that enables you unless an even more-specific explicit deny exists.
samir: pseudocode I keep in the internal docs (copy here for clarity):

```
function isFlagOn(request):
  for scope in [model, route, project, org]:
    cfg = lookupFlag(scope)
    if cfg is explicit boolean: return cfg
    if cfg has audience/rollout: return evaluate(cfg, request)
  return default_off
```

This makes "explicit deny wins at higher specificity" simple and predictable.
taylor: yup that matches runtime. also note: we treat multiple audience rules within the same scope as OR (if any audience matches, that scope returns true).
kyle: thanks, super helpful. last Q: who needs to sign off before I flip the project canary? do we need SRE/infrastructure guardrails?
anita: ping @samir for infra approval. also please: add the canary monitor, a short rollout plan in the PR, and a route-level kill-switch already set to OFF for the checkout route so we can rollback instantly. :thumbsup:
samir: I'll add the alert and a rollback playbook. infra-bot: please schedule the canary monitor for payments/feature_x 10% for 30m.
infra-bot: scheduled monitor: payments/feature_x canary 10% for 30m. monitor id m-7821. (reacted :white_check_mark:)
